question: True or false: in the European Union, a German-made hard cheese may not be sold under the name parmesan?
answer: True. In 2008 the European Court of Justice held that parmesan evokes Parmigiano Reggiano, a protected designation of origin, so within the EU the word belongs to cheese made to its rules in a zone around Parma and Reggio Emilia. Outside Europe it is widely treated as generic: an American supermarket shelf holds dozens.
move: A name that is common in one market can be property in another.
trap: Treating the English word as generic because it is everywhere.
reference: Case C-132/05, Commission v Germany, Court of Justice of the European Communities, judgment of 26 February 2008
